clue.text: Tell of number given to soldiers

indicators.note: given to places the number after the soldiers it is handed to, so the soldiers come first

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, stands for soldiers in crosswords
to count is to number, used here as a noun for a tally

explanation.surface: Someone reports the headcount of troops allotted to a unit.
explanation.definitionFit: To recount a story is to narrate or relate it in detail.

clue.text: Bob's on fire — it's his night!

parts.note: Bob is a short form of the first name Robert
something on fire burns

explanation.surface: A man called Bob is ablaze on his big night.
explanation.walkthrough: Burns Night on 25 January celebrates the Scottish poet with haggis and whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish poet is honoured each year on Burns Night, his own evening of celebration.

clue.text: Rough cut of meat — it comes out of pity

parts.note: a chop is a cut of lamb or pork

indicators.note: comes out of says one word is removed from inside another

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A butcher remarks that a poor cut of meat is a shame.
explanation.definitionFit: Choppy describes rough water with short broken waves.

clue.text: Subject to promise adopting student is hell

parts.note: under means subject to, as in under orders

indicators.note: adopting means taking in another piece, so one word holds the other

parts.note: your word is your promise
L for learner stands for a student

explanation.surface: A pledge that takes on a pupil turns out to be hellish.
explanation.definitionFit: The underworld is the realm of the dead, Hades or hell in mythology.

clue.text: Heat these initially on top of oven

indicators.note: in a down clue on top of places one piece above the other
initially means the first letter of these

parts.note: an oast is a kiln for drying hops

explanation.surface: Instructions to warm things up first on the top of the cooker.
explanation.walkthrough: An OAST is a kiln for drying hops, familiar in the English county of Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: To toast is to brown or warm something by heat.

clue.text: Shot a couple of legionnaires for rustling

parts.note: a crack is the sharp report of a gunshot

indicators.note: a couple of letters means the first two letters of the next word are taken

explanation.surface: Two soldiers of the Foreign Legion are executed for stealing cattle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' looks like a verb in a firing-squad story and 'rustling' like cattle theft; both are nouns here.
explanation.definitionFit: A rustling sound of dry leaves or paper is a series of small snapping noises.

clue.text: Rituals welcoming the Queen's clients

indicators.note: welcoming means taking a piece in, so one word holds the other

parts.note: customs are traditional rituals or practices
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: Ceremonies greeting a monarch's patrons.
explanation.definitionFit: Customers are the clients or patrons of a business.

clue.text: Part of America created so much land

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A remark on how much territory America made.
explanation.definitionFit: An acre is a unit of land measure, roughly 4,047 square metres.

clue.text: American state or county fortunate having no leader

parts.note: Kent is a county in south-east England

indicators.note: having no leader means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: lucky means fortunate

explanation.surface: Asks whether a US state or an English county is luckier when leaderless.
explanation.definitionFit: Kentucky is a state in the southern United States.

clue.text: Delighted about English victory, getting promoted

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round the others

parts.note: elated means delighted

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled by an English win gains promotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Being elevated means being raised in rank or status.

clue.text: Children are moody

definitions.meaning: a family's offspring collectively, like a hen's chicks
to sulk and dwell gloomily on something

explanation.definitionFit: A brood is a family of young, and to brood is to sulk or ponder gloomily.

clue.text: Uses car with an awful confidence

indicators.note: awful suggests the letters are in a terrible mess and need rearranging

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone drives a car with dreadful self-belief.
explanation.definitionFit: Assurance is self-confidence, a positive certainty in oneself.

clue.text: Amends allowance offered to poor padre, with no doubt initially

indicators.note: offered to puts the allowance after the reworked priest it is handed to
poor indicates the letters are in bad shape and must be reworked
the first letter of doubt is removed from the word padre

parts.note: a ration is a fixed allowance of food or supplies

explanation.surface: A struggling priest is offered a stipend as compensation, without hesitation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no doubt initially' removes D, leaving PARE, which 'poor' turns into a new order before the allowance follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Reparation is compensation paid to make amends for a wrong.

clue.text: Fish barrel — heart of oak

parts.note: a tun is a large cask for wine or beer

indicators.note: heart of means the central letter of the word oak

explanation.surface: Fish is packed in an oak barrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuna is a large ocean fish, often tinned.

clue.text: Wandering around, need margin to be flexible

indicators.note: flexible means bendable, so the letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: Advice that a wandering route needs room for manoeuvre.
explanation.definitionFit: Meandering means winding about aimlessly, like a river.

clue.text: Bird that's an emblem of Wales — and that's soup!

parts.note: a cock is a male bird, especially a rooster
i.e. (id est) means that is
the leek is a national emblem of Wales
i.e. again for that is

explanation.surface: A bird representing Wales is unexpectedly revealed to be a soup.
explanation.walkthrough: IE is the abbreviation of Latin id est, 'that is'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a Scottish soup of chicken and leeks.

clue.text: Rugby team become jerks when driving

definitions.meaning: the Australian national rugby league side's nickname
a learner's car lurches forward in bounds

explanation.walkthrough: To kangaroo is informal for a car moving in jerks, as when a learner mishandles the clutch.
explanation.definitionFit: The Australian rugby league team is nicknamed after the bounding animal, and a car that jerks forward hops like one.

clue.text: Have a bit of fun with projection for plant

parts.note: to lark about is to have fun
a spur is a projecting point

explanation.surface: Messing about with a protruding piece of a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Larkspur is a flowering garden plant, a kind of delphinium.

clue.text: Instrument's at home, covered in red wine

indicators.note: covered in means one piece is wrapped around another

parts.note: claret is red Bordeaux wine
in means at home

explanation.surface: A musical instrument lies at home soaked in red wine.
explanation.definitionFit: The clarinet is a single-reed woodwind instrument.

clue.text: Slay England, struggling around the beginning of union in the distant past

indicators.note: around means the scrambled letters surround another piece
struggling suggests the letters are thrashing about into a new order
the beginning of means the first letter of union

explanation.surface: A football match long ago in which a side beat a floundering England near the start of a union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' turns SLAY ENGLAND into AULDLANGSYNE minus U; 'around' puts U (beginning of union) inside it. The Scots phrase literally means 'old long since'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scots phrase means times long gone, days of long ago.

clue.text: Sigh drunkenly, eating a good dish

indicators.note: eating means taking in another piece
drunkenly means the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone sighs tipsily while eating a fine dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunkenly' rearranges SIGH to HGIS, split around AG by 'eating'. HAGGIS is a Scottish dish of offal in a stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: Haggis is a Scottish dish of sheep's offal and oatmeal.

clue.text: Revolutionary and best newspaper?

parts.note: red stands for a communist or revolutionary
top means best

explanation.surface: Asks whether a radical and excellent paper exists.
explanation.walkthrough: A red-top is a British tabloid, from its red masthead.
explanation.definitionFit: A red-top is a British tabloid paper, named for its red masthead.

clue.text: Marker buoy around edge

indicators.note: around here says the answer lies in the letters round the gap between the words

explanation.surface: A marker buoy floats around the edge of the water.
explanation.definitionFit: A kerb is the raised edge of a pavement, British spelling of curb.

clue.text: Crystalline rock soap for example, and sponge

parts.note: marble is metamorphic rock of recrystallised limestone
soap comes in a cake, a solid block

explanation.surface: A list of materials: rock, soap and a bath sponge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sponge' suggests the bathroom with soap, but it is a sponge cake.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a sponge cake swirled with two colours of batter.

clue.text: See 1
Sun's beginning without end

indicators.note: without end means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a start is a beginning

explanation.surface: Remark on a sunrise that never ends.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sun is a star, the one at the centre of our solar system.

clue.text: Point out no one runs to get wine

indicators.note: out signals the word point is put out of order

parts.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral I is one
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone observes that nobody runs to fetch the wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Point out' reads as one phrase meaning indicate, but 'out' is the anagram signal on the first word alone.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a red grape and the red wine made from it, famous in Burgundy.

clue.text: Bar that's popular with ghosts, oddly

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: oddly means the odd-numbered letters of ghosts are kept

explanation.surface: A pub that is a favourite haunt of ghosts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' looks like a pub; it is a bar of metal.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingot is a cast bar of gold or other metal.

clue.text: Regime gets disheartened and goes for profits

indicators.note: disheartened means the inner letters of regime are removed, leaving the outside pair

parts.note: a turn is a go, so goes means turns

explanation.surface: A government loses heart and changes direction in pursuit of gain.
explanation.definitionFit: Returns are the yield or profit on an investment.

clue.text: Notice drink becomes a part of the armed forces

definitions.text: becomes a part of the armed forces

parts.note: a sign is a notice displayed publicly
to sup is to drink, here as a noun

explanation.surface: A poster advertising drink persuades someone to enlist.
explanation.definitionFit: To sign up is to enlist formally in military service.
